column2: The Call of the Dark Gods

The skalds sing of Kjörn and Loesh, of Nierg and Tchar, and of the Snow King and the Great Bear beside them, as if all of them were the same. They are not. The old gods of the north grow fat on our gifts and give nothing back. The Dark Gods give. They give strength to the strong, wisdom to the cunning and long life to those who do not flinch from rot.\n\nI have heard their call long enough. Tonight I burn the old totems and give myself to the true powers of the world. To which of them shall I swear?

The herd has bellowed to all the Dark Gods alike, and the Dark Gods have answered all of us alike. That is no longer enough for me. One of them has whispered to me alone, and the warband that serves that god has marked me as its own. It is time to give my whole soul to one master.
Blood for the Blood God! Skulls for the Skull Throne!
Slaanesh will grant me every desire.
This world reeks of death. Grandfather Nurgle will keep me.
Everyone plots against me. The Changer of Ways shows me their plots.
All of them! For the Dark Gods, for Chaos Undivided!

At the runestone above the fjord the godi has laid out the totems of the north: the bull of Kjörn, the serpent of Loesh, the toad of Nierg, the raven of Tchar, the wolf of Olric and the bear of Órsen. A chieftain gives gifts to all the gods, but the greatest chieftains raise one god above the rest, and that god walks beside them in battle.\n\nThe law of my realm lets me raise only some of them. Whose totem shall I take up?
The bull. Kjörn, Lord of Battle, give me blood and skulls.
The serpent. Loesh will give me everything I crave.
The toad. Nierg, Father of Plagues, make me endure.
The raven. Tchar sees every secret and every road.
The wolf. Olric, Snow King, High King of the gods.
The bear. Órsen, Father of Bears, give me courage.
Not yet. All the gods shall have their gifts a while longer.
